goal: Map the current landscape of AI agents in scientific workflows for a discussion with DOE x-ray and neutron facility scientists, delivered as a self-contained HTML report with an appendix and verified references
run: Keep working across turns toward done_when below. After each turn, check done_when against what you have surfaced in this conversation — the evaluator reads conversation text only and cannot run tools or read files. If any item is not demonstrably met in surfaced text, continue, treating the unmet item as the next turn's directive. When all items are met, stop. Do not stop early on partial progress; do not exceed the bound. (In Claude Code, /goal automates exactly this loop.)

operating_mode.role: You are an orchestrator. Each iteration (= one turn): think about the next slice of work, decompose it, delegate to subagents via the Agent tool, then integrate. Doing small steps yourself is allowed; delegating is preferred. The decomposition is part of the deliverable. Audience: DOE x-ray and neutron facility scientists (SLAC, ORNL, BNL) plus university collaborators; pitch depth and Q4 to them. Prefer primary sources (papers, preprints, lab and project pages) over press coverage, and report the state as of the run date. For online lookups, use the endpoints in .externals/preprint_servers.json alongside web search: the arXiv API, Crossref, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar for papers and reference checks, and OSTI.GOV for DOE work relevant to Q4; follow each entry's rate-limit notes.
operating_mode.budget: Delegate to at least 3 and at most 6 subagents per iteration.
operating_mode.iterations: Complete at least 2 iterations before done_when may be considered met, even if it appears satisfied earlier — use surplus iterations to verify and harden.
operating_mode.ledger: Maintain agents-in-science-workflow/.goal/agents-science-workflow.ledger.json on disk, appending one FULL entry per iteration: {n, thought, delegated: [{agent, task, model}], integrated, new, remaining} — the file keeps every field. 'new' must name a decision or artifact that did not exist before this iteration. At the end of EVERY turn print a LEDGER digest (NOT the whole file): a header line `LEDGER agents-science-workflow — iterations N/2, full at agents-in-science-workflow/.goal/agents-science-workflow.ledger.json` (N = completed-iteration count); then one roster line per completed iteration `n · delegated:k · new: <that iteration's non-empty new>` (k = subagents delegated that iteration); then the current iteration's full JSON entry in a fenced block. Only the printed report shrinks; the file loses nothing. The evaluator reads conversation text only: what this turn's digest does not show does not exist, even if the file does.
operating_mode.claims: Maintain agents-in-science-workflow/.goal/agents-science-workflow.claims.json on disk — the campaign's key claims (typically 5–15), updated every iteration as claims land or change. Shape: {goal, slug, claims: [{id, provenance, evidence, claim}]} — goal and slug are set at bootstrap, keep them. provenance is one of: verified — evidence cites a checkable artifact you surfaced yourself in this conversation (script output you printed from your own run, a paper or page you fetched yourself); inherited — the evidence you hold is a report rather than the artifact: an external source, or a subagent's account of its own work (name the agent and task). Output a subagent quoted to you stays inherited until you re-run it yourself; inferred — reasoning only (evidence may describe partial support). Tags are lookups against the campaign record, never confidence scores. The final turn prints the complete file via cat.

done_when: agents-in-science-workflow/findings.html answers six questions with numbered in-text citations, each of Q1–Q6 citing at least 3 references: Q1 Landscape — a taxonomy of AI agent systems across the scientific workflow (literature and ideation, hypothesis, experiment design and self-driving labs, data analysis and simulation, writing and review), focused on 2024–2026, placing at least 25 named systems by stage and autonomy level; Q2 What works — peer-reviewed or independently reproduced results kept separate from claims, plus what the main benchmarks show about current capability; Q3 Infrastructure — models, agent frameworks, tool protocols such as MCP, and how agents connect to workflow and HPC systems; Q4 Facilities — agents at DOE x-ray and neutron user facilities and national labs (beamline and experiment steering, facility data analysis, DOE programs); Q5 Failure modes and risks — reproducibility, fabricated citations or results, evaluation gaps, safety and dual use, credit and authorship; Q6 Discussion — 6 to 10 open questions for the session, each tied to evidence from Q1–Q5. It also has an appendix (a system catalog with name, organization, year, stage, autonomy, evidence type and reference; a glossary; method notes) and a numbered reference list. Proven by printing the final-turn output of `python agents-in-science-workflow/check_report.py`, showing for each of Q1–Q6 its one-line answer and the reference numbers it cites, the catalog row count (at least 25), the discussion-prompt count (6 to 10), and a line confirming the catalog, glossary and method-notes sections are present.
findings.html is self-contained, proven by the same run printing `external resources loaded: 0` — no external scripts, stylesheets, fonts or images; outbound links to references are allowed.

Every reference is real and every citation closes, proven by the same run printing `references: N | resolved: N | failed: 0 | uncited: 0 | dangling: 0` with N ≥ 30 — resolved means confirmed in that run (DOIs via Crossref or doi.org, arXiv IDs via the arXiv API, other URLs fetched), with the fetched title matching the listed title for every DOI and arXiv ID.

The final turn prints the complete contents of agents-in-science-workflow/.goal/agents-science-workflow.claims.json via cat, showing: non-empty goal and slug; at least 1 entry in claims; every entry's provenance one of verified/inherited/inferred; every verified or inherited entry with non-empty evidence, each verified entry's evidence citing an identifier that appeared earlier in this conversation.

This turn prints the LEDGER digest — a header line reading iterations N/2 with N ≥ 2, one roster line per completed iteration each showing delegated:k with 3 ≤ k ≤ 6 and naming a non-empty 'new', and the current iteration's full JSON entry — showing at least 2 completed iterations.
guardrails: Create or modify files only under agents-in-science-workflow/ (its .goal/ folder included).
Do not write audience members' names or email addresses into any file — this repo is published on GitHub Pages; describe the audience by institution and field only.
Respect each source's terms of use and rate limits (e.g. arXiv about 1 request per 3 s).
bound: OR: the printed digest's header shows 9 completed iterations. In that case print the digest, the complete claims file via cat, and a gap report listing every unmet done_when item, then stop — this counts as bounded termination.
